nodes.characterization_summary: (Ni, Fe)3S2/NF and Ni3S2/NF display almost the same high-resolution Ni 2p and S 2p spectra.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S9. (a) High-resolution XPS spectra of (Ni, Fe)3S2/NF and Ni3S2/NF in the region of the (a) Ni 2p level and (b) S 2p level. The (Ni, Fe)3S2/NF and Ni3S2/NF display the almost same high-resolution Ni 2p and S 2p spectrums.

nodes.characterization_summary: (Ni, Fe)3S2/NF electrode displays charge transfer resistance R1 = 0.06 Ω, smaller than NFF (R1 = 0.24 Ω) and Raney Ni (R1 = 0.12 Ω), indicating faster electron transfer process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S10. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of (Ni, Fe)3S2/NF, Ni3S2/NF, NFF and Raney Ni. The inset shows an electrical equivalent circuit model. The (Ni, Fe)3S2/NF electrode displays a smaller charge transfer resistance (R1 = 0.06 Ω) than those of NFF (R1 = 0.24 Ω) and Raney Ni (R1 = 0.12 Ω), indicating that the former catalyst has a faster electron transfer process.
